text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Rollout alert: deploy 2026-03-15T21:00Z wave=1 -> service=inference-gateway reported elevated 5xx rate (2.3% over baseline) and health-check failures on 3/5 canary instances. Auto-safety policy triggered: paused further waves.

incident-bot: Paging on-call: alice-oncall (primary) and ben-sre (secondary). Runbook: infra/deployments/rollout-failure. Incident channel created.

alice-oncall: I'm on it. quick check — are the 5xxs concentrated on a single AZ or across regions?

carla-engineer: Seeing errors in logs from the new kernel selection path on these instances, stack trace points to kv-cache index mismatch on short sequences. Happened after the quantization change in the build.

alice-oncall: OK. impact assessment: can we estimate user-facing failures vs retries? metrics?

carla-engineer: Most are transient 502/504 from the gateway to runtime. Retries are causing increased latency for streaming sessions. Estimated ~0.7% of global requests currently failing to completion (from synthetic canary metrics).

jamie-cs: Any paid customers impacted yet? I can start a hold pattern for Affected Customer outreach once we have confirmation.

alice-oncall: Yes please stand by, jamie. We're treating this as P2 (service degradation for a subset). Priorities: 1) Stop rollout / ensure no more machines join wave 1 2) Undo the model runtime change on canaries (rollback or opt-out) 3) Route traffic away from failing instances 4) Notify CS+support for customers.

carla-engineer: We can flip the runtime feature flag that enabled the new kernel path. Quick safe rollback is to disable flag 'runtime.kernels.new_selection' for the deployment and trigger a soft restart of canaries.

alice-oncall: Good. Is that console-only or can we do via CLI? Give command.

carla-engineer: CLI is faster. Run: 

```
redwoodctl feature-flag set --env prod --flag runtime.kernels.new_selection --value off --target deployment:inference-gateway-wave1
redwoodctl rollout restart --deployment inference-gateway-wave1 --graceful
```

alice-oncall: Doing that now. I will annotate the deployment with incident id.

deploy-bot: Received command, applying flag change...

deploy-bot: Feature flag update accepted. Rolling restart queued for 3 canary instances.

alice-oncall: Routing change: I'm adding a temporary traffic rule to divert production traffic away from wave1 canaries to stable pool. Patch: set traffic_weight(wave1)=0 for 10m.

carla-engineer: Adding the command, will watch logs.

```
# temp traffic adjustment
redwoodctl traffic set --deployment inference-gateway --wave wave1 --weight 0
```

ben-sre: Noted. I'll start a quick check of downstream queues and autoscaler to ensure no overload when we shift traffic. Also confirming cloud provider health shows no AZ-level issues.

alice-oncall: jamie-cs can start drafting a short note: "We're seeing increased transient errors for a small fraction of requests to the inference API due to a rollout; we've paused the rollout and are rolling back the runtime change. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA." Keep it high level.

jamie-cs: On it. Draft: "We've paused a recent rollout after detecting an increased error rate impacting a small proportion of requests. Our engineers have rolled back the change for affected instances and traffic has been rerouted to stable capacity. If you are seeing errors, please retry; if issues persist let us know and we'll prioritize." Want me to send to customers now or wait for confirmation?

alice-oncall: Wait for confirmation of successful rollback and metrics stabilizing. Call out any enterprise customers with active incidents once we confirm.

carla-engineer: Canaries are restarting now. Watching logs...

```
[2026-03-15T21:02:12Z] inference-gateway-wave1-3: kv-cache index recovered, kernel selection fallback engaged
[2026-03-15T21:02:45Z] inference-gateway-wave1-2: restart complete, healthcheck=pass
[2026-03-15T21:03:01Z] inference-gateway-wave1-1: restart complete, healthcheck=pass
```

carla-engineer: Healthchecks passed for all restarted canaries. Error rate on wave1 instances dropping.

deploy-bot: Traffic weights updated: wave1=0. Safety: further waves remain paused.

alice-oncall: Metrics check: global 5xx rate back down to baseline (0.12%). Latency 95th also normalizing. I will mark the incident as mitigated and prepare the handoff to ben-sre for postmortem / RCA.

ben-sre: Taking over for RCA. Action items I've captured: 1) Collect runtime logs across both kernel paths 2) Reproduce locally with the exact quantized model + short sequences 3) Add more robust fallback in kernel selector to avoid kv-cache mismatch 4) Improve canary health detection thresholds to catch this earlier.

alice-oncall: Thanks. jamie-cs — you can now send the customer note. Also flag any customer support tickets that should be routed to engineering.

jamie-cs: Sent initial update to affected customers and created a ticket for the enterprise accounts team to follow up.

alice-oncall: Final operational notes: rollout paused by auto-policy at 21:00Z, feature flag disabled at 21:01Z, canary restarts completed by 21:03Z, traffic diversion applied at 21:04Z, error rate normalized by 21:06Z. Moving to status: mitigated -> monitoring. Adding checklist for postmortem.

ben-sre: I'll run the RCA meeting tomorrow morning, invite list: carla-engineer, alice-oncall, runtime-team, product-owner. I'll also open a postmortem doc and assign follow-ups.

alice-oncall: Handoff complete to ben-sre. If anything regresses ping this thread and I'll re-engage. Thanks all for the fast responses. :thumbsup:

jamie-cs: Closing customer comms loop, will follow up after root cause summary.

incident-bot: Incident record updated: severity=P2, mitigated=true, mitigation_timeline_added=true, assignee=ben-sre.

carla-engineer: Quick note for RCA: attach the failing run logs and the exact model artifact hashes; looks like a mismatch between the quantized artifact and the kernel optimizer.

ben-sre: Copy. Creating follow-up tasks now.

alice-oncall: Logged handoff and incident closure notes. Out.
